Illegal wood cutting

By: Anina Peens | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Illegal wood logging causing devastation of the Magaliesberg world heritage site

Unique Selling Point:
It takes 5 minutes to chop down a tree, but it takes it 25 years to grow back. The Magaliesberg Biosphere world heritage site is slowly losing the battle against illegal wood poachers who sell wood they claim originates from Botswana when in actual fact, they have teams of people chopping down trees seven days a week.

Summary:
The Pelindaba crossing between the Gauteng and North West provinces, is notorious countrywide for selling illegal firewood. Buyers travel from Mbombela, Bloemfontein and as far as Durban to stock up on cheap firewood to resell in their respective provinces. Marketed amongst others as Hardwood, Rooibos and Bushveld Iron wood, the wood sellers here don’t operate small businesses. As soon as bakkies, trucks, minibuses and utility vehicles drive off with their daily loads, bakkies and trucks arrive to fill up the stock. This seems to be happening around the clock. Although the sellers tell you that they receive stock from Botswana every three days, the truth is, the wood is chopped in the Magaliesberg mountains, a UNESCO world heritage site and protected biosphere.

Further information:
Complaints of private landowners between Rustenburg and Pretoria have increased in recent months to the Magaliesberg biosphere protection council. It has been reported that private fences are being cut to get access to trees in the area. This has frequently led to violent interactions between landowners and the illegal wood cutters. It is believed that a syndicate is operating in the area, employing Zimbabwean nationals.

If South Africans are not being made aware of the difference that exists between legal wood and illegal wood, the increase in demand for firewood will eventually lead to the destruction of the protected biosphere.


Story Elements

1. Government and the SAPS

The North West department of environmental affairs say their hands are tied. They have been the driving force in combating wood cutting and selling operations. In cooperation with Sanral and civil society, various raids have been carried out in the mountain. But apparently the cluster police commander in Brits, Brigadier Marx, halted all local police operations. We do not have an answer why this decision was taken, but this could be incorporated in an official interview with the police. NW Environmental affairs are now working on awareness campaigns to inform the public not support the illegal business.

2. National Bulk Supply

Every day of the week, people travel from as far as Durban to buy bulk supply of the wood at the low price of R10-R15 per bag. It is believed that this wood then enters the formal trade as legal wood. It is sold to petrol stations and general grocery dealers who do not question the origin. The Magaliesberg biosphere NGO is now in the process of erecting billboards to create awareness. They are also working on a plan to label wood that is legally packaged in order for the consumer to trace the origin. It is still a long and expensive way to go before they will see any success.

3. The Wood Sellers

Bylaws are not being enforced by the police to combat the retail business on the streets. When operations were still carried out by the local police authority in collaboration with SANRAL, SANRAL confiscated the wood. The sellers then started to send women and children in to sell the wood from the street. They sit at the stalls accompanied by children so the police cannot arrest them.

4. The Wood Cutter

People who have confronted the wood cutters say, “those people will kill you if you take away their chain saws”. They cut wood every day, seven days a week. They are most prevalent in the Hartbeespoort area and have cut down most of the trees in the protected valley areas around the town. We have footage of the woodcutters trying to throw down drones that located their whereabouts.

5. Alternative solutions

The reality is that the demand for firewood exist especially during summer, as most South Africans light up braais over weekends. It is also necessary to look at possible alternative income sources for the wood sellers, as this is their bread and butter.
The Magaliesberg biosphere trust believes that if government is willing to regulate the wood industry, solutions can be found. This include the cutting down and replanting of alien and invasive species, such as Jakaranda trees. Farm and landowners should also work with the government in availing wood chopped down on private land for resale.

We also visit a legal wood depot in Hartbeespoort to explore the difference between the wood sold legally, and the wood sold illegally. We can demonstrate this by making an actual fire. Nice visuals!


Extra Budget Items:
Dianah Chiyangwa went in to do the undercover investigation. There is a cost of R2000 attached to this.

Script:


Illegal Wood Script

MASA
“We all love a good braai, but did you know that some of the wood that you are buying could actually be illegal?”

VO
Not a lot of people question the origin of wood when picking up a bag for a braai.
As a consumer, you have the right to ask about the origin of the wood you are buying if there is no sticker or detail on the packaging that enables you to trace the source.
Because what people may not realize is that a wood purchase could be supporting a massive illegal firewood operation based near Hartbeespoort dam in the North West Province.

MASA:
“This is the Pelindaba crossing linking Gauteng and the North West provinces, it is synonymous with the sale of cheap firewood and bulk buyers come from all over the country to stock up right here”

VO
Wood sold here travel to various provinces as far as Durban, about 600km from Pelindaba. Vehicles are loaded to the brim and as soon as they drive off, a new load replaces the sale.
While vendors claim the wood is delivered monthly from the Limpopo province, the massive demand cannot rely on a monthly delivery. Opportunists have therefore found alternative yet, illegal sources of supply. Although they don’t have permits to fell trees, they are chopping up the Magaliesberg biosphere, a world protected UNESCO heritage site. The law prohibits anyone to cut down indigenous and protected trees in a biosphere.

UPSOUND
WOOD SELLER: YOU CAN’T JUST TAKE PHOTOS
MASA: BUT NO, HE IS GOING TO PUT IT DOWN, LET ME EXPLAIN TO YOU…
WOOD SELLER: NO, I DON’T LIKE IT

VO
Various raids on the entire operation have been performed pre lockdown, and vendors are aware that their trade is illegal and consequently they lie about the origin of the wood when confronted. Here, they are delivering Karee wood, but the wood is marked Hard wood or Mopani.

UPSOUND
WOOD SELLER AT TRUCK
MASA: “And where does all the wood come from?”
WOOD SELLER: It comes from Thabazimbi, Limpopo”
MASA: “It comes from Limpopo?”

VO
SUPER@ NAAS GROVE, PRESIDENT: SA DENDROLOGIST SOCIETY
“The Karee wood does not come from Limpopo, it is a species that occurs in the Magaliesberg biosphere, you can see the wood is freshly cut”

VO
Naas Grove is the president of the South African dendrologist society and says, green trees from the biosphere are constantly supplying the mass demand for firewood.

SUPER@ NAAS GROVE, PRESIDENT: SA DENDROLOGIST SOCIETY
“This is Rushed bush willow”
WOOD SELLER: “Ja exactly”
MASA: “But it is under the Dry Mopani”
WOOD SELLER: “It goes like Mopani, that is why it is being sold as Mopani, but Mopani you won’t get it around here”

VO
The mass deforestation of the Magaliesberg biosphere has been happening for over five years, but after the lockdown, locals say the operation has exploded.

MASA:
“A Biosphere is not a reserve, it is not a place where animals are kept in and people out, in fact, people must be involved to help conserve and not destroy this specific area”

SUPER@BELINDA COOPER, MAGALIESBERG BIOSPHERE RESERVE
“This is an incredibly unique place on earth and there are not any other places like this on earth in terms of the natural and cultural heritage that has such a deep history in this area”

VO
Belinda Cooper, coordinator of the Magaliesberg biosphere Reserve says the uncontrolled harvesting may finally lead to a complete extinction of species that are unique to this region.

SUPER@BELINDA COOPER, MAGALIESBERG BIOSPHERE RESERVE
“There are eight eco system types of which three are critically endangered. And they are occurring in the Magaliesberg particularly where this wood harvesting is such a problem”.

VO
Cooper says the problem stretches across the Magaliesberg region between Pretoria and Rustenburg and that the Hartbeespoort dam is the hardest hit.

SUPER@ NAAS GROVE, PRESIDENT: SA DENDROLOGIST SOCIETY
“Look at this, you can start counting, we just passed about six stalls and there is another two three four five seven nine ten, just in a matter of 500 meters we have 10 different outlets.

VO
We sent an undercover journalist to spend a day with some of the vendors at the Pelindaba depot. It is believed that all the vendors use the same supplier.

SUPER@UNDERCOVER JOURNALIST PLEASE SUBTITLE
“I found that this is a group of people come from one province in Zimbabwe.”
Masa: So all the vendors are foreign nationals?
Journalist: All of them.

VO
From Pelindaba across the entire Hartbeespoort area all the wood sold are cut in the same size blocks, packaged in the same type of plastic and sealed in a similar way.

MASA
“So, I just had a chat with this family who say they actually go up into the mountain to go and chop wood themselves, he also said that he goes into private land to chop the wood but alleges that he has permission from the landowners.”

VO
But some landowners in the area say, they don’t permit this and that their fences are being cut and their properties intruded.

SUPER@LANDOWNER PLEASE MASK VOICE AND BLUR FACE WHERE YOU CAN SEE HIM
“Just to give you an idea, this road we are walking on wasn’t here. This road has been carved out by illegal wood cutters in the area”

VO
This landowner removed tons of chopped wood from his property after he succeeded in chasing the loggers away. The heaps of sawdust are testimony to the mass destruction of indigenous trees in the area.

MASA:
“So much for hard wood from Limpopo”

VO
Some landowners claim they have been attacked with pangas and chain saws upon confrontation with the loggers.
This drone was used by a local resident to trace the whereabouts of the cutters in the mountain behind Hartbeespoort town.
Residents say, they hear the chainsaws on a daily basis, every day of the week.

INSERT BETTER QUESTION Masa: Property owners say they wake up to find wood heaps like these on their properties, what do you do?

SUPER@LANDOWNER PLEASE MASK VOICE AND BLUR FACE WHERE YOU CAN SEE HIM
“In certain times you do actually stumble upon the perpetrators and in order to confront them, it is a situation that you just don’t want to be in, let’s put it that way”

VO
Cooper says the biosphere reserve receives complaints on a daily basis while Grove says he has been reporting the problem many times.

SUPER@ NAAS GROVE, PRESIDENT: SA DENDROLOGIST SOCIETY
“I have been watching this story for five years now and I have reported it to various departments now, the Green scorpions, the department of environmental affairs but nothing ever happened to any one of these people.”

SUPER@ BASIE DIOLE, DEDECT
“We’ve had several complaints from members of the public including foreigners, to say people are cutting green trees within the Magalies biosphere, as a result we organized a blitz.
VO
The provincial department of economic development environment conservation and tourism, or DEDECT say they are at wits end with the fight against the illegal operation.

SUPER@ BASIE DIOLE, DEDECT
“We confiscated stacks and stacks of firewood, I think more than 10 tons of trucks took away firewood to Pretoria where they stored it”
SUPER@ BASIE DIOLE, DEDECT
“We went up this mountain, what we saw there can make you cry. These people are chopping off all the trees.” INSERT DRONE VISUALS

VO
Diole says although the vendors claim they are poor and battling to make a living, the entire wood business is estimated to turn more than a million Rand in profit monthly. He added that the operation is likely to be the work of a syndicate.

SUPER@ BASIE DIOLE, DEDECT
“You can see this thing is organized, if people have chain saws and equipment and all manners of things cutting down the trees. You can see it is an organized thing.”

VO
DEDECT say it has been an uphill battle to get support from the local police.

SUPER@ BASIE DIOLE, DEDECT
“I have spoken to them, I forwarded them submissions, kindly requesting to give us the necessary support, thus far nothing came.”

VO
SAPS North West say they have not been able to provide support recently as lockdown regulations have tied their hands.

SUPER@BRIGADIER SABATA MOKGWABONE, SPOKESPERSON: NORTH WEST SAPS
“We had a lack of resources, it was lockdown… it as level 3…we need to prioritize…
BACK TO BACK
SUPER@BRIGADIER SABATA MOKGWABONE, SPOKESPERSON: NORTH WEST SAPS
…But We are part of this thing, we know about it, we are aware about it.”

VO
Although the provincial SAPS claim they are in control of the situation, our undercover journalist found that some police members are being bribed by vendors in order not to get arrested for trespassing, breaking bylaws, operating without permits and breaking international legislation and provisions of the national forestry act.

SUPER@UNDERCOVER JOURNALIST
“While I was sitting there a police car pulled up…. And they drove off with wood…”

VO
The wood sellers say the only way they can remain in business is if the police work with them.

UPSOUND
MASA: “So you don’t have a permit to sell?”
WOOD SELLER: “No we don’t have”
MASA: “So when the police comes here do, they ever ask you for your permits?”
WOOD SELLER: “No when they come, they just take wood”
MASA: “Oh so the police come, they don’t ask for permits, they take the wood instead?”
WOOD SELLER: “Yes they take it”
MASA: “So it is your deal with the police?”
WOOD SELLER: “It is not our deal”
MASA: “So it is your supplier’s deal?”
WOOD SELLER: “Yes”

VO
The provincial police say these bribes will not be tolerated.

SUPER@BRIGADIER SABATA MOKGWABONE, SPOKESPERSON: NORTH WEST SAPS
“I think I have made it clear that we do not actually condone corruption within our ranks”

VO
North West SAPS concluded that raids are currently being planned.

The bush cutters are believed to move from area to area between raids. They stay in groups in various areas far up in some of the most inhabitable cliffs, where the old trees that have grown here for centuries are at risk of being sliced up.

VO
Even if the police raid the vendors, the cutters are hard to catch. But if the demand decreases, it may be the first step in curbing the mass deforestation. Government, civil society and landowners are pleading with consumers to buy responsibly in order to prevent the complete devastation of the world’s oldest mountain range.

MASA: “So much for hard wood from Limpopo” VO Some landowners claim they have been attacked with pangas and chain saws upon confrontation with the loggers. This drone was used by a local resident to trace the whereabouts of the cutters in the mountain behind Hartbeespoort town. Residents say, they hear the chainsaws on a daily basis, every day of the week. INSERT BETTER QUESTION Masa: Property owners say they wake up to find wood heaps like these on their properties, what do you do? SUPER@LANDOWNER PLEASE MASK VOICE AND BLUR FACE WHERE YOU CAN SEE HIM “In certain times you do actually stumble upon the perpetrators and in order to confront them, it is a situation that you just don’t want to be in, let’s put it that way” VO Cooper says the biosphere reserve receives complaints on a daily basis while Grove says he has been reporting the problem many times. SUPER@ NAAS GROVE, PRESIDENT: SA DENDROLOGIST SOCIETY “I have been watching this story for five years now and I have reported it to various departments now, the Green scorpions, the department of environmental affairs but nothing ever happened to any one of these people.” SUPER@ BASIE DIOLE, DEDECT “We’ve had several complaints from members of the public including foreigners, to say people are cutting green trees within the Magalies biosphere, as a result we organized a blitz. VO The provincial department of economic development environment conservation and tourism, or DEDECT say they are at wits end with the fight against the illegal operation. SUPER@ BASIE DIOLE, DEDECT “We confiscated stacks and stacks of firewood, I think more than 10 tons of trucks took away firewood to Pretoria where they stored it” SUPER@ BASIE DIOLE, DEDECT “We went up this mountain, what we saw there can make you cry. These people are chopping off all the trees.” INSERT DRONE VISUALS VO Diole says although the vendors claim they are poor and battling to make a living, the entire wood business is estimated to turn more than a million Rand in profit monthly. He added that the operation is likely to be the work of a syndicate. SUPER@ BASIE DIOLE, DEDECT “You can see this thing is organized, if people have chain saws and equipment and all manners of things cutting down the trees. You can see it is an organized thing.” VO DEDECT say it has been an uphill battle to get support from the local police. SUPER@ BASIE DIOLE, DEDECT “I have spoken to them, I forwarded them submissions, kindly requesting to give us the necessary support, thus far nothing came.” VO SAPS North West say they have not been able to provide support recently as lockdown regulations have tied their hands. SUPER@BRIGADIER SABATA MOKGWABONE, SPOKESPERSON: NORTH WEST SAPS “We had a lack of resources, it was lockdown… it as level 3…we need to prioritize… BACK TO BACK SUPER@BRIGADIER SABATA MOKGWABONE, SPOKESPERSON: NORTH WEST SAPS …But We are part of this thing, we know about it, we are aware about it.” VO Although the provincial SAPS claim they are in control of the situation, our undercover journalist found that some police members are being bribed by vendors in order not to get arrested for trespassing, breaking bylaws, operating without permits and breaking international legislation and provisions of the national forestry act. SUPER@UNDERCOVER JOURNALIST “While I was sitting there a police car pulled up…. And they drove off with wood…” VO The wood sellers say the only way they can remain in business is if the police work with them. UPSOUND MASA: “So you don’t have a permit to sell?” WOOD SELLER: “No we don’t have” MASA: “So when the police comes here do, they ever ask you for your permits?” WOOD SELLER: “No when they come, they just take wood” MASA: “Oh so the police come, they don’t ask for permits, they take the wood instead?” WOOD SELLER: “Yes they take it” MASA: “So it is your deal with the police?” WOOD SELLER: “It is not our deal” MASA: “So it is your supplier’s deal?” WOOD SELLER: “Yes” VO The provincial police say these bribes will not be tolerated. SUPER@BRIGADIER SABATA MOKGWABONE, SPOKESPERSON: NORTH WEST SAPS “I think I have made it clear that we do not actually condone corruption within our ranks” VO North West SAPS concluded that raids are currently being planned. The bush cutters are believed to move from area to area between raids. They stay in groups in various areas far up in some of the most inhabitable cliffs, where the old trees that have grown here for centuries are at risk of being sliced up. VO Even if the police raid the vendors, the cutters are hard to catch. But if the demand decreases, it may be the first step in curbing the mass deforestation. Government, civil society and landowners are pleading with consumers to buy responsibly in order to prevent the complete devastation of the world’s oldest mountain range.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Illegal wood logging causing devastation of the Magaliesberg world heritage site
metadata.Unique Selling Point: It takes 5 minutes to chop down a tree, but it takes it 25 years to grow back. The Magaliesberg Biosphere world heritage site is slowly losing the battle against illegal wood poachers who sell wood they claim originates from Botswana when in actual fact, they have teams of people chopping down trees seven days a week.
metadata.Summary: The Pelindaba crossing between the Gauteng and North West provinces, is notorious countrywide for selling illegal firewood. Buyers travel from Mbombela, Bloemfontein and as far as Durban to stock up on cheap firewood to resell in their respective provinces. Marketed amongst others as Hardwood, Rooibos and Bushveld Iron wood, the wood sellers here don’t operate small businesses. As soon as bakkies, trucks, minibuses and utility vehicles drive off with their daily loads, bakkies and trucks arrive to fill up the stock. This seems to be happening around the clock. Although the sellers tell you that they receive stock from Botswana every three days, the truth is, the wood is chopped in the Magaliesberg mountains, a UNESCO world heritage site and protected biosphere.
metadata.Further information: Complaints of private landowners between Rustenburg and Pretoria have increased in recent months to the Magaliesberg biosphere protection council. It has been reported that private fences are being cut to get access to trees in the area. This has frequently led to violent interactions between landowners and the illegal wood cutters. It is believed that a syndicate is operating in the area, employing Zimbabwean nationals. If South Africans are not being made aware of the difference that exists between legal wood and illegal wood, the increase in demand for firewood will eventually lead to the destruction of the protected biosphere. Story Elements 1. Government and the SAPS The North West department of environmental affairs say their hands are tied. They have been the driving force in combating wood cutting and selling operations. In cooperation with Sanral and civil society, various raids have been carried out in the mountain. But apparently the cluster police commander in Brits, Brigadier Marx, halted all local police operations. We do not have an answer why this decision was taken, but this could be incorporated in an official interview with the police. NW Environmental affairs are now working on awareness campaigns to inform the public not support the illegal business. 2. National Bulk Supply Every day of the week, people travel from as far as Durban to buy bulk supply of the wood at the low price of R10-R15 per bag. It is believed that this wood then enters the formal trade as legal wood. It is sold to petrol stations and general grocery dealers who do not question the origin. The Magaliesberg biosphere NGO is now in the process of erecting billboards to create awareness. They are also working on a plan to label wood that is legally packaged in order for the consumer to trace the origin. It is still a long and expensive way to go before they will see any success. 3. The Wood Sellers Bylaws are not being enforced by the police to combat the retail business on the streets. When operations were still carried out by the local police authority in collaboration with SANRAL, SANRAL confiscated the wood. The sellers then started to send women and children in to sell the wood from the street. They sit at the stalls accompanied by children so the police cannot arrest them. 4. The Wood Cutter People who have confronted the wood cutters say, “those people will kill you if you take away their chain saws”. They cut wood every day, seven days a week. They are most prevalent in the Hartbeespoort area and have cut down most of the trees in the protected valley areas around the town. We have footage of the woodcutters trying to throw down drones that located their whereabouts. 5. Alternative solutions The reality is that the demand for firewood exist especially during summer, as most South Africans light up braais over weekends. It is also necessary to look at possible alternative income sources for the wood sellers, as this is their bread and butter. The Magaliesberg biosphere trust believes that if government is willing to regulate the wood industry, solutions can be found. This include the cutting down and replanting of alien and invasive species, such as Jakaranda trees. Farm and landowners should also work with the government in availing wood chopped down on private land for resale. We also visit a legal wood depot in Hartbeespoort to explore the difference between the wood sold legally, and the wood sold illegally. We can demonstrate this by making an actual fire. Nice visuals!
